title: Bio signals: hepatitis B, uveitis, Ebola and coverage costs
summary: Today’s edition covers a new hepatitis B treatment approval, Phase 3 uveitis results, Nigeria’s imported Ebola case and a reported 9% rise in workers’ family health coverage costs.

stories.headline: FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment
stories.dek: The FDA approved bepirovirsen with existing antiviral therapy for a defined group of adults with chronic hepatitis B.
tldr: The FDA approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) with existing antiviral therapy for certain adults with chronic hepatitis B who do not have cirrhosis.
The agency said 24% of treated patients in two trials met criteria to stop their existing medicine, compared with none receiving placebo.
The label includes a boxed warning for serious liver reactions and low platelet counts; the approval does not apply to all people with hepatitis B.

body.text: The FDA said it approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen), in combination with existing antiviral therapy, for certain adults with chronic hepatitis B who do not have cirrhosis. Eligible patients must have taken antiviral therapy for at least six months and meet specified viral-marker criteria.

The agency described Hibsago as the first FDA-approved antisense oligonucleotide for chronic hepatitis B. It is administered by injection for up to 24 weeks alongside existing medicine, which patients continue for at least 24 weeks after the last Hibsago dose.

Across the two trials cited by FDA, 24% of patients receiving Hibsago met requirements to stop their existing medicine, compared with none receiving placebo. Twenty-four weeks after stopping all hepatitis B treatment, 19% still had controlled virus with hepatitis B surface antigen undetectable.

The FDA label carries a boxed warning for serious liver reactions and low platelet counts, as well as other warnings. The approval is limited to the labeled patient group, and the long-term durability of treatment-free control remains a question for follow-up evidence.

stories.whyItMatters: The decision introduces an antisense option into a treatment area where many patients have relied on long-term suppression. Its restricted eligibility, required combination therapy and safety monitoring define how narrowly the evidence can be applied.
stories.editorNote: Regulatory details and trial percentages are taken from FDA materials; no patient-specific treatment conclusions are implied.

stories.headline: Brepocitinib meets all Phase 3 end points in noninfectious uveitis
stories.dek: Roivant and Priovant reported positive results from two Phase 3 studies; the indication has not been approved.
tldr: Roivant and Priovant said brepocitinib met the primary endpoint in both CLARITY Phase 3 trials for noninfectious uveitis.
The company-reported studies enrolled 166 and 204 participants, and treatment failure by week 48 was lower in the brepocitinib groups than in placebo groups.
The results are topline company disclosures; regulatory review and full peer-reviewed reporting remain pending.

body.text: Roivant and its subsidiary Priovant reported positive topline results from CLARITY-1 and CLARITY-2, two Phase 3 trials of brepocitinib for noninfectious uveitis. The companies said the primary endpoint was met in both studies.

The sponsor reported that the trials enrolled 166 and 204 participants. At week 48, cumulative treatment failure was 35.4% with brepocitinib versus 78.7% with placebo in CLARITY-1, and 32.4% versus 77.8% in CLARITY-2.

The company also reported higher rates of steroid-free quiescence at week 48 in the treatment groups than in the placebo groups. These are sponsor-reported topline findings; the announcement does not substitute for a full peer-reviewed publication or regulator assessment.

Brepocitinib is already approved for dermatomyositis under the LISRAYA brand, according to the coverage. The noninfectious uveitis use remains investigational, and the companies said they intend to seek an additional indication in 2027.

stories.whyItMatters: The results could support expansion of an existing drug into an inflammatory eye disease, but they remain a sponsor-reported clinical milestone. Regulatory review and detailed publication will determine how the topline efficacy and safety findings are interpreted.
stories.editorNote: Trial outcomes are attributed to company disclosures and reported coverage; no treatment guidance is offered.

stories.headline: Nigeria confirms imported case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease
stories.dek: The WHO says a patient in Abuja tested positive after recent travel to Uganda; authorities identified 44 contacts and are tracing exposures.
tldr: Nigeria confirmed one imported Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease case in Abuja, the fifth country to report the virus in the outbreak that began in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The WHO said the patient had recently travelled to Uganda, tested positive on October 20 and was receiving care in isolation; investigators were still tracing travel and exposure history.
Nigeria reported 44 contacts under monitoring, while Africa CDC called a regional meeting for October 28 as cases continued to be reported across several countries.

body.text: Nigeria confirmed one imported case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory, according to the World Health Organization’s regional office. The WHO said the patient was a woman with recent travel to Uganda and that a laboratory test confirmed the virus on October 20.

The WHO reported that symptoms began on October 7, four days after the patient arrived in Nigeria, and that she sought care at a private Abuja facility on October 11. She was in isolation and receiving medical care; investigators were still establishing her likely infection source and reconstructing her travel and exposure history.

The Nigerian health ministry reported 44 contacts identified and monitored, and said infection-control measures were being intensified at the facility. The Associated Press reported that most contacts were health workers and that the patient’s spouse was also among them.

The WHO described Nigeria as the fifth country to detect the virus since the Democratic Republic of the Congo outbreak was declared on May 15. The Associated Press reported that Africa CDC invited health ministers to an extraordinary virtual meeting scheduled for October 28; the extent of onward transmission from the imported case remained under investigation.

stories.whyItMatters: The confirmed case expands the outbreak’s geographic footprint and places emphasis on case investigation, contact monitoring and coordination between national health authorities and regional agencies. The WHO said the source and exposure history were still under investigation, so the route and onward transmission risk were not yet fully established.
stories.editorNote: Added in the 19:00 KST same-date merge, using WHO reporting and independent Associated Press coverage. No clinical or prevention advice is included.

stories.headline: Workers are paying 9% more for family health coverage this year, a higher jump than in the recent past
stories.dek: A KFF survey found the average worker contribution for family coverage rose to $7,471 in 2026.
tldr: Workers’ average contribution toward employer family health coverage reached $7,471 in 2026, up 9% from 2025, according to KFF survey findings reported by STAT and Axios.
The annual survey covered more than 1,900 employers and found employers are responding with measures such as onsite clinics and direct negotiations with health systems.
The reported increase describes employer-sponsored coverage and does not represent every worker’s premium or other forms of insurance.

body.text: Workers paid an average of $7,471 toward family health coverage through employers in 2026, a 9% increase from 2025, according to the annual KFF employer survey reported by STAT and Axios. The reported increase was larger than in the recent past.

KFF’s survey included more than 1,900 employers. STAT reported that the increase reflected higher family coverage costs for workers, while Axios described employers exploring ways to manage the expense.

Axios reported that some employers are establishing onsite clinics and negotiating directly with health systems. Those approaches were presented as employer responses to rising spending; the survey does not establish how broadly they are available or how much they reduce costs.

The $7,471 figure is an average worker contribution for employer-sponsored family coverage, not a universal household bill. The reports do not imply that every employee faced the same increase or describe costs for individual-market, public or other coverage.

stories.whyItMatters: Employer health coverage is a major channel through which medical cost changes reach workers and businesses. The 9% figure signals a higher reported worker contribution in this survey, while its employer-sponsored scope limits how far it can be generalized to all insured households.
stories.editorNote: Added in the 19:00 KST same-date merge. Figures are attributed to KFF’s employer survey as reported by STAT and Axios; no health or insurance advice is offered.
